question: A pilot of a Claude-assisted proposal workflow has produced mixed results across its first month. Which two iteration steps are appropriate now? Select two.
options: A) Compare the weak outputs against the strong ones to find what the weak requests were missing.
B) Roll the workflow out to every team at once so that far more data arrives much faster.
C) Abandon the pilot right away, because a mixed opening month shows the workflow cannot ever work.
D) Fold what worked into the shared instructions so the whole team gets the same improvement.
E) Ask each person to keep a private list of tricks rather than changing the shared set-up.
correct_answers: A) Compare the weak outputs against the strong ones to find what the weak requests were missing.
D) Fold what worked into the shared instructions so the whole team gets the same improvement.
explanations: Correct. Comparing weak and strong cases diagnoses the cause instead of guessing, which is what iteration on a pilot is for.
Incorrect. Scaling an unresolved pilot spreads the failure mode rather than diagnosing it, and it makes rollback harder.
Incorrect. Mixed results in month one are the normal input to iteration, not proof that the workflow is unworkable.
Correct. Making the fix persistent in shared instructions stops the team re-solving the same problem one person at a time.
Incorrect. Private tricks leave the shared configuration untouched, so the improvement never reaches anyone else.
